record.original_question: Is there a finitely presented, or even type F∞ , boundedly acyclic simple orderable group?

evidence.quote: Question 3.5. Is there a finitely presented, or even type F∞ , boundedly acyclic simple orderable group?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A discrete group $G$ is called boundedly acyclic if its bounded cohomology with trivial real coefficients vanishes in all positive degrees, that is, $H_b^n(G;\mathbb{R}) = 0$ for every $n \geq 1$. The group $G$ is called left-orderable (or orderable) if there exists a total order $\leq$ on $G$ that is invariant under left multiplication: $a \leq b$ implies $ga \leq gb$ for all $g,a,b \in G$. The group $G$ is simple if it has no nontrivial proper normal subgroups. The group $G$ is of type $F_\infty$ if it admits a classifying space (a $K(G,1)$) with finitely many cells in each dimension; in particular, type $F_\infty$ groups are finitely presented.

Question: Does there exist a finitely presented (or, more strongly, of type $F_\infty$) group $G$ that is simultaneously simple, left-orderable, and boundedly acyclic?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (e.g., on twisted Brin–Thompson groups and embedding theorems by Fournier-Facio, Lodha, Monod, Wu and others) has produced finitely generated simple boundedly acyclic groups, and finitely presented non-amenable boundedly acyclic groups, as well as finitely generated left-orderable simple groups. However, no construction simultaneously combining all four properties (finitely presented, boundedly acyclic, simple, and left-orderable) appears in the literature, and the question is posed as open.

status_evidence.title: Embedding groups into boundedly acyclic groups
status_evidence.snippet: Every finitely generated group embeds quasi-isometrically into a finitely generated boundedly acyclic simple group, via twisted Brin-Thompson groups.
status_evidence.claim: Finitely generated boundedly acyclic simple groups exist, but finite presentation combined with left-orderability remains unaddressed.

status_evidence.title: Bounded cohomology of finitely presented groups: vanishing, non-vanishing, and computability
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs a finitely presented non-amenable boundedly acyclic group.
status_evidence.claim: Finitely presented boundedly acyclic groups exist, but the constructions are not known to be simple and orderable.
